390	
391	**6.3 Plume Stability Assessment**
392	
393	Crestline reviewed historical groundwater monitoring data from sampling events conducted in 2005, 2008, 2011, 2014, 2017, and 2020 to assess plume stability and evaluate the effectiveness of the monitored natural attenuation remedial strategy. The following general trends were identified:
394	
395	**Source Area (MW-7):** PCE concentrations in the source area have demonstrated a declining trend, decreasing from approximately 85 μg/L in 2005 to 18 μg/L in October 2020. TCE concentrations in MW-7 have similarly decreased from approximately 22 μg/L in 2005 to 4.3 μg/L in 2020. The presence of cis-1,2-DCE (12 μg/L in 2020) and vinyl chloride (1.4 μg/L in 2020) at MW-7 is consistent with ongoing reductive dechlorination, indicating that natural attenuation processes are active in the source area.
396	
397	**Downgradient Plume (MW-9, MW-12):** PCE concentrations at MW-9 have fluctuated between approximately 4 and 9 μg/L over the monitoring period and do not demonstrate a clear declining trend. Vinyl chloride at MW-12 has fluctuated: 1.8 μg/L (2005), 4.2 μg/L (2011), 2.8 μg/L (2017), and 3.1 μg/L (2020). The vinyl chloride data at MW-12 does not show a clear declining trend and has exceeded the GWQS of 2 μg/L at the three most recent sampling events.
398	
399	**Property Boundary (MW-14):** PCE concentrations at MW-14 were 1.8 μg/L in 2014, 2.1 μg/L in 2017, and 2.4 μg/L in 2020. PCE concentrations at MW-14 show a slight increasing trend over the 2014--2020 period, though concentrations remain in the low μg/L range. MW-14 is located at the southeastern property boundary in the general direction of groundwater flow toward the southern property boundary where the freshwater wetland is located.
400	
401	**Plume Margins (MW-6, MW-10, MW-11, MW-13):** Concentrations at the lateral plume margin wells have remained below or near GWQS throughout the monitoring period, indicating that the plume has not significantly expanded laterally.
402	
403	Based on the available data, the dissolved-phase chlorinated solvent plume appears stable with a general decreasing concentration trend in the source area (the most recent data reviewed was from October 2020, approximately four years prior to this assessment). While source area concentrations have declined substantially, the downgradient and plume margin data indicate that the plume has not yet attenuated to below GWQS across the entire monitoring network. The vinyl chloride data at MW-12 and the PCE data at MW-14 indicate that conditions in the distal portions of the plume warrant continued monitoring attention.
404	
405	**[7.0 Vapor Intrusion Evaluation]{.underline}**
406	
407	**7.1 Screening Assessment**
408	
409	The Phase I ESA (August 12, 2024) identified potential vapor intrusion concerns as REC-2 for Buildings C and D, which are located directly above or adjacent to the historical groundwater plume centerline where dissolved-phase chlorinated solvents (PCE and TCE) have been detected at concentrations significantly above NJDEP GWQS. Buildings C and D are situated in the central portion of the Site overlying or adjacent to the footprint of the former solvent blending building (AOC-3).
410	
411	Under the NJDEP Vapor Intrusion Technical Guidance (Version 4.1, 2018), a vapor intrusion investigation is warranted when volatile organic compounds are present in groundwater beneath or near an occupied building at concentrations exceeding the NJDEP Vapor Intrusion Groundwater Screening Levels (\"VIGWSLs\"). The VIGWSL for PCE is 1 μg/L, and the VIGWSL for TCE is 1 μg/L. Concentrations detected at MW-7 during the October 2020 monitoring event (PCE at 18 μg/L; TCE at 4.3 μg/L) significantly exceed these screening levels. MW-7 is located in the immediate vicinity of Buildings C and D.
412	
413	Building C (58,000 square feet) is located directly above the footprint of the former Building 3 (AOC-3) and is situated within the CEA boundary. Building D (48,000 square feet) is located immediately adjacent to the eastern margin of the former Building 3 footprint and overlies the downgradient portion of the dissolved-phase groundwater plume. Both buildings are occupied by commercial tenants and are slab-on-grade construction, which may provide a preferential pathway for vapor intrusion in the absence of engineering controls or vapor barriers.
414	
415	Based on the proximity of Buildings C and D to the dissolved-phase groundwater plume, a vapor intrusion investigation consisting of sub-slab soil gas sampling and indoor air sampling is recommended for these two buildings.
416	
417	**7.2 Recommendations.** Crestline recommends that a vapor intrusion investigation be performed for Buildings C and D, consisting of the following scope of work:
418	
419	1\. Installation of sub-slab soil gas sampling points at a minimum of three locations per building, positioned to provide representative spatial coverage of the building footprint and to target areas where groundwater contamination concentrations are highest based on available monitoring well data.
420	
421	2\. Collection of sub-slab soil gas samples to be analyzed for volatile organic compounds by United States Environmental Protection Agency (\"USEPA\") Method TO-15.
422	
423	3\. Collection of indoor air samples from each building at locations representative of the occupied space, to be analyzed for volatile organic compounds by USEPA Method TO-15.
424	
425	4\. Collection of concurrent outdoor (ambient) air samples to establish background concentrations and to enable evaluation of potential indoor air contributions from ambient sources.
426	
427	5\. Comparison of analytical results to NJDEP Indoor Air Screening Levels and Soil Gas Screening Levels as set forth in the NJDEP Vapor Intrusion Technical Guidance (Version 4.1, 2018).
428	
429	The vapor intrusion investigation should be performed in accordance with the NJDEP Vapor Intrusion Technical Guidance (Version 4.1, 2018), including adherence to seasonal sampling considerations, building preparation protocols, and quality assurance/quality control requirements.
430	
431	**[8.0 Additional Environmental Features]{.underline}**
432	
433	**8.1 Freshwater Wetlands**
434	
435	A 2.8-acre freshwater wetland and associated 50-foot transition area was identified along the southern property boundary. The wetland is delineated under NJDEP Letter of Interpretation File No. 0418-02-0003.1 FWW, issued in 2002. The LOI confirmed the presence and boundaries of the wetland, which appears to be a freshwater emergent/scrub-shrub system associated with a tributary of the Green Brook. The wetland is classified as an exceptional resource value wetland under the New Jersey Freshwater Wetlands Protection Act (N.J.S.A. 13:9B), which mandates the 50-foot transition area as a protective buffer.
436	
437	The wetland is located along the southernmost extent of the Property, generally downgradient of the dissolved-phase chlorinated solvent groundwater plume. The Property boundary and associated wetland transition area constrain potential development or disturbance activities in this portion of the Site. No evaluation of potential impacts from site contamination to the wetland was conducted as part of this assessment.
438	
439	**8.2 Radon.** Somerset County, New Jersey, is classified as EPA Radon Zone 1, indicating the highest potential for elevated indoor radon levels. Zone 1 areas have predicted average indoor radon screening levels greater than 4 picocuries per liter (pCi/L), which exceeds the USEPA action level of 4 pCi/L. No radon testing was performed as part of this PA. Radon is a naturally occurring radioactive gas produced by the decay of uranium in soil and rock and is not related to the industrial contamination history of the Site. Radon testing is recommended as part of any building occupancy evaluation or renovation program.
440	
441	**8.3 Asbestos-Containing Materials and Lead-Based Paint**
442	
443	The Phase I ESA (August 12, 2024) identified the potential presence of asbestos-containing materials (\"ACM\") in pipe insulation in Buildings B and D, and the potential presence of lead-based paint (\"LBP\") in Building B. These conditions were identified as Business Environmental Risks (\"BERs\") in the Phase I ESA (designated BER-1 and BER-2, respectively). ACM and LBP are building material conditions that are not within the scope of the ASTM E1527-21 standard or the NJDEP Technical Requirements for Site Remediation and are not further evaluated in this PA. Pre-renovation and pre-demolition surveys for ACM and LBP are recommended prior to any renovation or demolition activities at the affected buildings.
444	
445	**[9.0 Deed Notice and Institutional Controls Review]{.underline}**
446	
447	**9.1 Deed Notice**
448	
449	A deed notice was recorded on March 14, 2003, in the Somerset County Clerk\'s Office as Document No. 2003-015892. The deed notice covers three Areas of Concern: AOC-1 (former underground storage tank area), AOC-3 (former solvent blending building), and AOC-5 (former drum storage yard). The deed notice is an institutional control mechanism approved by NJDEP as part of the remedial action for the Property under Case No. SRP-098742.
450	
451	The deed notice restricts use of the identified areas and requires maintenance of engineering controls (including pavement caps, building foundations, and other physical barriers) that serve as barriers to direct contact with residual soil contamination. Specifically, the deed notice prohibits any activities that would compromise the integrity of the engineering controls without prior NJDEP approval, prohibits residential use of the identified areas, and requires that any soil disturbance within the deed notice areas be conducted in accordance with a soil management plan. The deed notice runs with the land and is binding on all current and future property owners, lessees, and occupants. A copy of the deed notice is included in Appendix C.
452	
453	**9.2 Classification Exception Area (CEA)**
454	
455	A Classification Exception Area was established in 2003 for the dissolved-phase chlorinated solvent groundwater plume associated with NJDEP Case No. SRP-098742. The CEA restricts the use of groundwater within the defined plume boundary, prohibiting the installation of potable water supply wells or other groundwater extraction for consumptive use within the CEA boundary. The CEA is documented in NJDEP records and is associated with the approved monitored natural attenuation remedial strategy for the groundwater plume.
456	
457	CEA monitoring requirements include periodic groundwater sampling to confirm plume stability and compliance with the MNA remedial strategy. The monitoring program is intended to demonstrate that the plume is not expanding and that natural attenuation processes are reducing contaminant concentrations over time. The most recent sampling event documented in available records was conducted in October 2020.
458	
459	**9.3 Biennial Certification Status**
460	
461	Under the Site Remediation Reform Act (SRRA, N.J.S.A. 58:10C), the Licensed Site Remediation Professional of record is required to submit biennial certifications to NJDEP for sites with active institutional and engineering controls. The biennial certification confirms that the institutional and engineering controls established at the site --- including the deed notice and the CEA --- remain in place and are protective of human health and the environment. The biennial certification also requires the LSRP to evaluate whether the remedial action remains protective and to identify any changes in site conditions that may affect the protectiveness of the remedy.
462	
463	The most recent biennial certification on file with NJDEP was submitted on April 15, 2021. Biennial certifications are required every two years from the date of the prior submission. The biennial certification submitted in April 2021 concluded that the institutional and engineering controls at the Site remained in place and that the remedial action continued to be protective based on available data at that time. A copy of the April 2021 biennial certification is included in Appendix C.
464	
465	**[10.0 Conclusions and Recommendations]{.underline}**
466	
467	**10.1 Conclusions.** Based on Crestline\'s review and evaluation of existing environmental data for the Property at 200 Commerce Drive, Calverley, New Jersey, the following conclusions are presented for each Area of Concern and for the dissolved-phase groundwater plume:
468	
469	**AOC-1 (Former Underground Storage Tank Area):** Residual benzene contamination in soil (maximum 5.2 mg/kg in sample AOC1-S3) and groundwater (3.8 μg/L in MW-2) exceeds applicable NJDEP Non-Residential Direct Contact Soil Remediation Standards and Groundwater Quality Standards, respectively. AOC-1 is managed under the existing deed notice (Document No. 2003-015892). Post-excavation confirmation sampling during the 1998 UST removal was limited to the north and east excavation sidewalls; the south and west sidewalls were not sampled.
470	
471	**AOC-3 (Former Solvent Blending Building):** Post-SVE soil sampling indicates that soil at AOC-3 meets applicable Non-Residential Direct Contact Soil Remediation Standards. The area is managed under the existing deed notice. AOC-3 remains the identified source area for the dissolved-phase chlorinated solvent groundwater plume.
472	
473	**AOC-5 (Former Drum Storage Yard):** Soil analytical results at AOC-5 are below applicable NJDEP Non-Residential Direct Contact Soil Remediation Standards. The area is managed under the existing deed notice as a precautionary measure.
474	
475	**Dissolved-Phase Groundwater Plume:** The dissolved-phase chlorinated solvent plume appears generally stable based on available monitoring data from October 2020, with decreasing concentration trends observed in the source area. PCE, TCE, and vinyl chloride continue to exceed NJDEP GWQS in multiple monitoring wells across the plume footprint. Monitoring well MW-14, located at the southeastern property boundary, reports PCE at 2.4 μg/L, which exceeds the GWQS of 1 μg/L.
476	
477	**Overall:** Residual contamination associated with historical operations by Consolidated Solvents & Coatings, Inc. remains on the Property at concentrations above unrestricted-use standards. The Site is managed under existing institutional controls, including the recorded deed notice and the CEA. Data gaps exist as identified in Section 10.2 below.
478	
479	**10.2 Data Gaps and Recommendations**
480	
481	Based on the findings and conclusions of this Supplemental Preliminary Assessment, Crestline identifies the following data gaps and recommendations:
482	
483	1\. **Vapor Intrusion Investigation:** A vapor intrusion investigation is recommended for Buildings C and D, consisting of sub-slab soil gas and indoor air sampling, in accordance with NJDEP Vapor Intrusion Technical Guidance (Version 4.1, 2018). Buildings C and D are located above or adjacent to the dissolved-phase groundwater plume where chlorinated solvents have been detected at concentrations significantly exceeding the applicable VIGWSLs.
484	
485	2\. **1,000-Gallon Diesel UST (Near Building B):** The Phase I ESA identified a 1,000-gallon diesel UST near the northeast corner of Building B for which no NJDEP closure documentation was located. A geophysical survey (ground-penetrating radar or magnetometer) is recommended to confirm the presence or absence of the UST. If the UST is located, closure in accordance with N.J.A.C. 7:14B and investigation of potential impacts should be performed.
486	
487	3\. **Updated Groundwater Monitoring:** Crestline recommends that updated groundwater monitoring be considered to confirm current plume conditions. The existing monitoring well network (MW-1 through MW-14) provides adequate spatial coverage for a comprehensive sampling event. Updated data would support evaluation of ongoing natural attenuation effectiveness and current plume configuration.
488	
489	4\. **Deed Notice Compliance:** The existing deed notice and engineering controls should continue to be maintained in accordance with the terms of the deed notice (Document No. 2003-015892). Any planned construction, renovation, or soil disturbance within the deed notice areas should be coordinated with the LSRP of record and conducted in accordance with an approved soil management plan.
490	
491	**[11.0 Limitations and Qualifications]{.underline}**
492	
493	This Supplemental Preliminary Assessment was prepared for the exclusive use of Greenfield Capital Partners LLC and Thornbury & Marsh LLP in connection with Greenfield\'s proposed acquisition of the Property located at 200 Commerce Drive, Calverley, Somerset County, New Jersey 08807. No other party may rely on this report without the prior written consent of Crestline Environmental Consultants, Inc.
494	
495	This PA is based on a review of existing data and documents as described in Section 4.0. No field sampling, subsurface investigation, or site reconnaissance was conducted as part of this assessment. Environmental conditions may exist at the Property that are not identified in the records and reports available for Crestline\'s review. The absence of evidence of contamination in available records does not necessarily indicate the absence of contamination.
496	
497	Environmental conditions are dynamic and may change over time due to natural processes, human activities, or other factors. The conclusions and recommendations presented in this report are based on data and information available as of the report date (September 5, 2024) and are subject to revision as additional information becomes available.
498	
499	This PA does not constitute a Remedial Investigation or Site Investigation under N.J.A.C. 7:26E. The scope of this assessment is limited to a desktop evaluation of existing data and does not include the physical characterization of subsurface conditions. A Phase II Site Investigation, including field sampling and laboratory analysis, would be required to fully characterize environmental conditions at the Property.
500	
501	The opinions expressed herein are based on professional judgment and the information available at the time of the assessment. Crestline has exercised reasonable care in performing this assessment, consistent with generally accepted environmental consulting practices and the applicable standard of care in the State of New Jersey. No warranties, express or implied, are made regarding the findings, conclusions, or recommendations presented in this report.
502	
503	This report is subject to the terms and conditions set forth in the engagement letter between Crestline Environmental Consultants, Inc. and Thornbury & Marsh LLP, dated July 15, 2024.
504	
505	**[APPENDIX A: FIGURES]{.underline}**
506	
507	The following figures are provided in support of this Supplemental Preliminary Assessment:
508	
509	> • **Figure 1:** Site Location Map --- Shows the regional and local location of the Property within Calverley Township, Somerset County, New Jersey. Depicts major roadways, geographic features, and the Property boundary.
510	>
511	> • **Figure 2:** Site Plan --- Shows the Property boundary, building locations (Buildings A through E), AOC locations (AOC-1, AOC-3, and AOC-5), monitoring well locations (MW-1 through MW-14), the CEA boundary, the freshwater wetland and 50-foot transition area along the southern property boundary, and the approximate location of the undocumented 1,000-gallon diesel UST near Building B.
512	>
513	> • **Figure 3:** Historical Groundwater Plume Map --- Presents isoconcentration contour maps for PCE at three time periods: 1990 (Remedial Investigation), 2005, and October 2020. Illustrates the general configuration and extent of the dissolved-phase plume over time.
514	>
515	> • **Figure 4:** Groundwater Concentration Trend Graphs --- Presents time-series plots of PCE and TCE concentrations at key monitoring wells (MW-7, MW-12, and MW-14) from 2005 through October 2020.
516	>
517	> • **Figure 5:** Cross-Section A-A\' Through Plume Centerline --- Presents a generalized hydrogeologic cross-section through the plume centerline from the source area (AOC-3) to the southeastern property boundary, depicting subsurface geology, groundwater elevation, and dissolved-phase contaminant distribution.
518	
519	**[APPENDIX B: ANALYTICAL DATA TABLES (FULL LABORATORY REPORTS)]{.underline}**
520	
521	Full laboratory analytical reports for the October 2020 groundwater monitoring event and historical soil analytical reports for AOCs 1, 3, and 5 are included in Appendix B. Summary tables are presented in the text of this report (Tables 1 through 5). The laboratory reports include complete chain-of-custody documentation, analytical methodologies, detection limits, and quality assurance/quality control data.
522	
523	**[APPENDIX C: REGULATORY CORRESPONDENCE]{.underline}**
524	
525	Copies of key regulatory documents referenced in this report are included in Appendix C:
526

536	>

540	
541	Historical maps and aerial photographs reviewed in the preparation of this report are included in Appendix D:

The property is approximately 73% leased to 14 tenants, with the largest tenant being Apex Logistics Corp., which occupies Building A under a lease expiring December 31, 2026. The remaining tenants include various office, light warehouse, and professional services companies.
34	
35	The Subject Property is currently owned by Ridgeline Industrial Holdings, Inc., a New Jersey corporation, which has owned the property since 1997, when it acquired the site from the Chapter 7 bankruptcy estate of the former owner and operator. The Subject Property is zoned I-2 (General Industrial) under the Calverley Township zoning ordinance.
36	
37	Historical records indicate that the Subject Property was used for agricultural purposes from approximately 1920 to 1961. From 1962 to 1996, the property was owned and operated by Consolidated Solvents & Coatings, Inc., which conducted chemical blending, solvent recovery, and drum reconditioning operations at the site. These operations resulted in significant soil and groundwater contamination, which is the subject of ongoing regulatory oversight under New Jersey Department of Environmental Protection (\"NJDEP\") Case No. SRP-098742.
38	
39	Based on the records review, historical sources review, site reconnaissance, and interviews conducted as part of this Phase I ESA, Crestline has identified the following environmental conditions at the Subject Property:
40	
41	**Three Recognized Environmental Conditions (RECs):**
42	
43	**REC-1: Residual Chlorinated Solvent Contamination.** Residual chlorinated solvent contamination exists in soil and groundwater at the Subject Property associated with former Consolidated Solvents & Coatings, Inc. operations, specifically at AOC-1 (former underground storage tank area), AOC-3 (former solvent blending building), and AOC-5 (former drum storage yard). This contamination is the subject of NJDEP Case No. SRP-098742 and is managed under an existing deed notice (Document No. 2003-015892, recorded March 14, 2003, in the Somerset County Clerk\'s Office) and a Classification Exception Area (\"CEA\") established in 2003. Contamination levels remain above unrestricted-use soil remediation standards and NJDEP Groundwater Quality Standards in portions of the site.
44	
45	**REC-2: Potential Vapor Intrusion Concerns --- Buildings C and D.** Buildings C and D are located directly above or adjacent to the historical dissolved-phase chlorinated solvent groundwater plume as delineated in the 1990 Remedial Investigation. Volatile chlorinated solvents (tetrachloroethylene \[\"PCE\"\], trichloroethylene \[\"TCE\"\], and vinyl chloride) in groundwater can migrate as vapors through soil into overlying structures. No vapor intrusion investigation has been performed at the Subject Property. The absence of vapor intrusion data constitutes a data gap that prevents evaluation of whether these occupied structures are impacted by volatile chemical vapors from the underlying groundwater contamination.
46	
47	**REC-3: Undisclosed 1,000-Gallon Diesel Underground Storage Tank.** A 1,000-gallon diesel underground storage tank (\"UST\") was identified on a 1990 site plan contained in the NJDEP file for Case No. SRP-098742, located near the northeast corner of Building B. This identification is corroborated by the 1965 Sanborn fire insurance map. No closure documentation was found in NJDEP files or property records for this tank. The UST does not appear in NJDEP\'s UST registration database. The UST is not referenced in the existing deed notice, the 2001 Remedial Action Workplan, or any subsequent regulatory filings reviewed by Crestline. Ridgeline\'s representative stated he was unaware of the existence of this tank. The Seller\'s Environmental Disclosure Questionnaire dated July 28, 2024, states that \"all USTs have been properly closed and removed,\" which is inconsistent with the absence of closure records for this tank.
48	
49	**One Controlled Recognized Environmental Condition (CREC):**
50	
51	**CREC-1: Deed Notice and Classification Exception Area.** The existing deed notice (Document No. 2003-015892) and CEA for AOCs 1, 3, and 5 constitute a Controlled Recognized Environmental Condition. Contamination remains on-site above unrestricted-use standards but is managed under institutional and engineering controls implemented pursuant to NJDEP-approved remedial actions.
52	
53	**No Historical Recognized Environmental Conditions (HRECs) were identified.**
54	
55	**Two Business Environmental Risks (BERs):**
56	
57	**BER-1: Asbestos-Containing Materials (ACM).** Suspect asbestos-containing materials were observed in pipe insulation (thermal system insulation) in the mechanical rooms of Buildings B and D. No comprehensive asbestos survey in accordance with AHERA or NESHAP has been performed.
58	
59	**BER-2: Lead-Based Paint (LBP).** Lead-based paint is likely present in Building B, which retains structural elements from a pre-1978 warehouse with paint coatings on steel framing and wall surfaces. No LBP survey has been performed.
60	
61	Based on the findings of this Phase I ESA, Crestline recommends that a Phase II ESA be conducted to further evaluate the identified RECs. Specifically, Crestline recommends the following: (a) a subsurface investigation including a geophysical survey (ground-penetrating radar and/or magnetometry) and targeted soil and groundwater sampling to locate and assess the status of the 1,000-gallon diesel UST near Building B; (b) a vapor intrusion investigation consisting of sub-slab soil gas sampling and indoor air sampling in Buildings C and D in accordance with NJDEP\'s Vapor Intrusion Technical Guidance (October 2021); and (c) updated groundwater sampling from the existing monitoring well network to confirm current plume conditions.

137	**3.2 Site and Vicinity General Characteristics**
138	
139	**Total Acreage and Topography:** The Subject Property encompasses approximately 47.3 acres of land. The site topography is generally flat to gently sloping from northwest to southeast. Approximate surface elevations range from approximately 85 feet above mean sea level (North American Vertical Datum of 1988 \[\"NAVD88\"\]) in the northwestern portion of the site to approximately 72 feet NAVD88 along the southeastern boundary near the wetland area. The topographic gradient facilitates surface water drainage generally toward the south and southeast.
140	
141	**Geology:** Based on published geologic mapping and historical site investigation reports, the Subject Property is underlain by alluvial and glacial deposits consisting of sand, silt, clay, and gravel, ranging in thickness from approximately 10 to 25 feet below ground surface (\"bgs\"). These unconsolidated deposits overlie fractured shale and mudstone of the Brunswick Formation, part of the Newark Supergroup (Triassic--Jurassic age). The bedrock surface is irregular and generally encountered at depths of approximately 20 to 30 feet bgs based on historical boring logs from the 1990 Remedial Investigation.
142	
143	**Hydrology and Groundwater:** Groundwater in the overburden aquifer is encountered at depths of approximately 8 to 15 feet bgs based on historical monitoring well data collected during previous site investigations. Groundwater flow direction is generally to the southeast, consistent with the topographic gradient and the position of the unnamed perennial tributary to Green Brook along the southern property boundary. The unconsolidated alluvial deposits serve as the primary shallow aquifer. The fractured bedrock serves as a secondary aquifer, though no bedrock wells are documented on the property.
144	
145	A freshwater wetland system encompassing approximately 2.8 acres is located along the southern boundary of the property. This wetland is associated with the unnamed perennial tributary to Green Brook, which flows generally eastward along the southern margin of the site. The wetland is classified as PEM1C (Palustrine Emergent Persistent, Seasonally Flooded) per the National Wetlands Inventory (\"NWI\"). A 50-foot transition area, as required by the New Jersey Freshwater Wetlands Protection Act (N.J.S.A. 13:9B-1 *et seq.*), buffers the wetland from the developed portion of the site.
146	
147	**Utilities:** The Subject Property is served by municipal water supply from the Elizabethtown Water Company. There are no on-site potable water supply wells or irrigation wells. Sanitary sewer service is provided through a connection to the Somerset-Raritan Valley Sewerage Authority system. Stormwater is managed on-site through a permitted stormwater management system consisting of two detention basins, with discharge authorized under a New Jersey Pollutant Discharge Elimination System (\"NJPDES\") permit.

249	> **NJDEP UST Registration:** Three 10,000-gallon underground storage tanks are registered with NJDEP under the following registration numbers: NJ-UST-093241 (gasoline), NJ-UST-093242 (gasoline), and NJ-UST-093243 (waste solvent). All three tanks were registered to Consolidated Solvents & Coatings, Inc. The status of all three registrations is \"Permanently Closed -- Removed\" (1998), consistent with the removal of the tanks by Ridgeline during the 1998 redevelopment. No registration record was found in NJDEP\'s UST database for a 1,000-gallon diesel underground storage tank at the Subject Property.
250	>
251	> **NJDEP Underground Storage Tank Database (BUST):** Consistent with the UST registration records, the NJDEP Bureau of Underground Storage Tanks database lists three closed (removed) USTs at the Subject Property. No record of a diesel UST was identified in this database.
252	>
253	> **NJ Spill Database:** Four spill incidents were reported at the Subject Property, all associated with operations conducted by Consolidated Solvents & Coatings, Inc.: (i) a 1978 solvent release during drum handling; (ii) a 1982 UST overfill incident; (iii) a 1985 process wastewater discharge to ground; and (iv) a 1991 release from a leaking underground pipe. All four spills are reported as \"Closed\" in NJDEP records, and the associated contamination is encompassed within the ongoing NJDEP Case No. SRP-098742.
254	
255	**Adjoining and Nearby Property Listings:**
256	
257	The database search included all federal and state databases within the applicable ASTM E1527-21 search radii for adjoining and nearby properties. The following is a summary of notable findings:
258	
259	  -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
260	  **Property**                       **Database**   **Status**          **Distance / Direction**   **Concern to Subject Property**
261	  ---------------------------------- -------------- ------------------- -------------------------- ------------------------------------------------------------
262	  180 Commerce Drive (dry cleaner)   KCSL           Active              \~500 ft NW                No --- groundwater flow to SE (away from Subject Property)
263	
264	  310 Industrial Way                 BUST (UST)     Closed -- Removed   \~1,200 ft E               No --- closed UST with NFA
265	
266	  Commerce Drive Office Park         NJ Spill       Closed              \~800 ft N                 No --- minor spill, closed
267	  -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
268	
269	No properties identified within the applicable search radii were listed on databases at a status that would be expected to affect the Subject Property, with one exception: a dry cleaning facility at 180 Commerce Drive (approximately 500 feet northwest of the Subject Property) is listed on the NJDEP KCSL with a tetrachloroethylene (\"PCE\") groundwater impact. However, based on the regional groundwater flow direction (to the southeast, i.e., away from the Subject Property), this off-site source is not considered to represent a REC for the Subject Property.
270	
271	**5.1.2 NJDEP File Review.** Crestline reviewed a partial case file for NJDEP Case No. SRP-098742, obtained via an Open Public Records Act (\"OPRA\") request submitted on July 8, 2024, and through the NJDEP DataMiner online portal. As noted in Section 2.4, the complete case file was not available due to ongoing OPRA processing delays. Crestline reviewed all documents that were available as of the report date. Key documents reviewed are summarized below and copies are provided in Appendix E.
272	
273	**Documents Reviewed:**
274	
275	> \(a\) Administrative Consent Order (\"ACO\") dated 1987, issued by NJDEP to Consolidated Solvents & Coatings, Inc., requiring the performance of a remedial investigation and interim remedial measures at the site.
276	>
277	> \(b\) Remedial Investigation (\"RI\") Report dated 1990, prepared by Atlas Environmental Services (now defunct), on behalf of Consolidated Solvents & Coatings, Inc. The RI addressed soil and groundwater contamination at the site, including delineation of the dissolved-phase chlorinated solvent groundwater plume.
278	>
279	> \(c\) Remedial Action Workplan (\"RAW\") submitted by Ridgeline Industrial Holdings, Inc. in 2001, proposing a modified remedial approach including monitored natural attenuation (\"MNA\") for the dissolved-phase groundwater plume and institutional/engineering controls for residual soil contamination.
280	>
281	> \(d\) Deed notice recorded March 14, 2003, Somerset County Clerk\'s Office, Document No. 2003-015892, encumbering AOC-1, AOC-3, and AOC-5.
282	>
283	> \(e\) Classification Exception Area (\"CEA\") documentation dated 2003, establishing a groundwater use restriction over the defined plume boundary.
284	>
285	> \(f\) Biennial certification dated April 15, 2021 (most recent on file), submitted under the Site Remediation Reform Act (\"SRRA\").
286	
287	**Key Regulatory History:**
288	
289	> **1984:** NJDEP case opened following the discovery of chlorinated solvent contamination in monitoring wells installed as part of a state-directed investigation. Elevated concentrations of tetrachloroethylene (\"PCE\"), trichloroethylene (\"TCE\"), and associated volatile organic compounds (\"VOCs\") were detected in soil and groundwater samples.
290	>
291	> **1987:** NJDEP issued an Administrative Consent Order (\"ACO\") to Consolidated Solvents & Coatings, Inc., requiring the company to conduct a comprehensive remedial investigation and implement interim remedial measures to address the contamination.
292	>
293	> **1990:** Atlas Environmental Services completed the Remedial Investigation (\"RI\") on behalf of Consolidated. The RI identified a dissolved-phase chlorinated solvent plume in the overburden groundwater originating from the central portion of the site (vicinity of the former solvent blending building, now AOC-3) and extending toward the southeast. The plume was approximately 1,200 feet long and 400 feet wide at its maximum extent, as mapped based on the distribution of PCE, TCE, and vinyl chloride (a degradation product of TCE) at concentrations exceeding NJDEP Groundwater Quality Standards (\"GWQS\"). The RI also identified soil contamination at three principal Areas of Concern: AOC-1 (former UST area), AOC-3 (former solvent blending building), and AOC-5 (former drum storage yard).
294	>
295	> **June 1994 -- November 1996:** A soil vapor extraction (\"SVE\") system was installed and operated at AOC-3 to address VOC-contaminated soil in the vadose zone beneath and around the former solvent blending building. The SVE system operated for approximately 30 months and removed an estimated 14,200 pounds of VOCs from the subsurface.
296	>
297	> **1996:** Consolidated Solvents & Coatings, Inc. ceased operations and filed for Chapter 7 bankruptcy (Case No. 96-BK-34521, U.S. Bankruptcy Court, District of New Jersey). The SVE system was decommissioned following the cessation of operations.
298	>
299	> **1997:** Ridgeline Industrial Holdings, Inc. acquired the property from the bankruptcy estate for \$2,400,000. Ridgeline assumed responsibility for environmental compliance at the site.
300	>
301	> **1998:** Three 10,000-gallon USTs (two gasoline, one waste solvent) were removed from AOC-1 under NJDEP oversight. Post-excavation soil sampling was conducted.
302	>
303	> **1998--2003:** Ridgeline demolished the former industrial structures and redeveloped the site into the current commercial park configuration with five buildings. Ridgeline submitted the RAW in 2001, and NJDEP approved a modified remedial approach including monitored natural attenuation for the dissolved-phase groundwater plume and institutional/engineering controls (deed notice and engineering controls) for residual soil contamination at AOC-1, AOC-3, and AOC-5. The deed notice was recorded on March 14, 2003, and the CEA was established in 2003.
304	>
305	> **2003--Present:** The site has been managed under the institutional and engineering controls established pursuant to the NJDEP-approved remedial approach. Groundwater monitoring has been conducted periodically, and biennial certifications have been filed under SRRA. The most recent biennial certification on file with NJDEP is dated April 15, 2021.
306	
307	Under the Site Remediation Reform Act (\"SRRA\"), the Licensed Site Remediation Professional (\"LSRP\") of record for an active NJDEP case is required to submit biennial certifications to NJDEP confirming that institutional and engineering controls remain protective of human health and the environment and that the remedy continues to function as designed.
308	
309	**1,000-Gallon Diesel UST --- 1990 Site Plan:**
310	
311	The 1990 site plan reviewed as part of the NJDEP file for Case No. SRP-098742 depicts a 1,000-gallon diesel underground storage tank located near the northeast corner of the structure corresponding to the current Building B location. This UST is labeled on the site plan as \"1000 gal diesel UST.\" The tank is not referenced in the Administrative Consent Order (1987), the Remedial Investigation Report (1990), the Remedial Action Workplan (2001), the deed notice (2003), or any subsequent regulatory correspondence or filings reviewed by Crestline. No NJDEP closure documentation --- including UST closure notification forms, tank removal records, post-removal soil sampling results, or closure certification letters --- was identified for this tank in the available case file or in NJDEP\'s UST registration database. A copy of the relevant portion of the 1990 site plan is provided in Appendix E.
312	
313	**5.2 Historical Use Information**
314	
315	**5.2.1 Sanborn Fire Insurance Maps.** Crestline reviewed Sanborn fire insurance maps for the Subject Property and vicinity for the following years: 1930, 1950, 1965, 1975, and 1985. Copies of the reviewed Sanborn maps are provided in Appendix D.
316	
317	**1930 Map:** The Subject Property is depicted as agricultural land, identified as a dairy farm. No structures are shown on the property. The surrounding area is depicted as primarily agricultural with scattered residential properties.
318	
319	**1950 Map:** The Subject Property remains depicted as agricultural land with the same general configuration as shown on the 1930 map. No industrial or commercial structures are present on the property. Minor residential development is visible to the west.
320	
321	**1965 Map:** The Subject Property is depicted with industrial structures and is labeled \"Consolidated Solvents & Coatings\" and \"Chemical Blending & Drum Reconditioning.\" Multiple buildings and structures are shown, including a solvent blending building (labeled \"Building 3\" in the central portion of the site), storage buildings, and support structures. Underground storage tanks are depicted in the northwestern portion of the site (corresponding to AOC-1). A drum storage yard is shown in the southeastern portion of the site (corresponding to AOC-5). Notably, a notation of \"1000 gal diesel tank\" appears near the northeastern corner of a warehouse structure corresponding to the approximate location of the current Building B. This notation corroborates the depiction of the 1,000-gallon diesel UST on the 1990 NJDEP site plan.
322	
323	**1975 Map:** The Subject Property shows expanded operations compared to the 1965 map. Additional above-ground storage tanks are visible. The drum storage yard in the southeastern portion appears expanded, with additional drum storage areas delineated. Notations indicate solvent recovery operations in the central portion of the site. The warehouse near the northeast corner of the site continues to be depicted; however, the 1,000-gallon diesel tank notation is not repeated on this edition.
324	
325	**1985 Map:** The Subject Property appears substantially similar to the 1975 map. No significant changes to the configuration of structures or operations are evident. The site remains labeled as Consolidated Solvents & Coatings with chemical blending and drum reconditioning operations.
326	
327	**5.2.2 Historical Aerial Photographs.** Crestline reviewed historical aerial photographs of the Subject Property and vicinity for the following years: 1940, 1957, 1970, 1979, 1986, 1995, 2005, and 2015. An index of the reviewed aerial photographs is provided in Appendix D.
328	
329	**1940:** The Subject Property appears as agricultural land with cultivated fields. No structures are visible on the property, other than possible farm outbuildings in the far northwest corner of the property that are partially obscured.
330	
331	**1957:** The property continues to appear as agricultural land. A cluster of farm buildings is visible in the northwest corner of the site. The surrounding area remains predominantly agricultural.
332	
333	**1970:** Industrial development is evident on the Subject Property. Multiple buildings and structures are visible, consistent with the development depicted on the 1965 Sanborn map. Cleared and graded areas are visible in the southeastern portion of the site. Drum storage areas are discernible as rows of containers or drums in the central and southeastern portions.
334	
335	**1979:** The aerial photograph shows what appears to be peak industrial activity at the site. Above-ground storage tanks are clearly visible. Material stockpiles and drum storage areas are visible across the central and southeastern portions of the site. The wetland area along the southern boundary is visible, with mature vegetation apparent.
336	
337	**1986:** The property appears substantially similar to the 1979 aerial. Possible areas of soil disturbance are evident in the southeastern portion of the site near the current location of AOC-5 (former drum storage yard). The surrounding area shows increased commercial and residential development to the north and west.
338	
339	**1995:** The site appears partially inactive. Some structures appear to be in disrepair or partially demolished, consistent with the cessation of operations by Consolidated Solvents & Coatings in 1996. Drum storage areas appear reduced in extent.
340	
341	**2005:** The current commercial park configuration is visible. The five existing buildings (A through E) are present. Former manufacturing structures have been demolished. Paved parking areas and landscaped areas are visible. The stormwater management basins are discernible.
342	
343	**2015:** No significant changes from the 2005 configuration are evident. The property appears well-maintained and consistent with commercial office and light warehouse use.
344	
345	**5.2.3 City Directory Review.** Crestline reviewed city directories (R.L. Polk & Co. and Cole Directories) for the Subject Property address. Consolidated Solvents & Coatings, Inc. is listed at 200 Commerce Drive from 1963 through 1996, with a Standard Industrial Classification (\"SIC\") Code of 2899 (Chemicals and Chemical Preparations, Not Elsewhere Classified). Ridgeline Industrial Holdings, Inc. is listed at the same address from 1998 onward, with a general classification as a commercial real estate management company.
346	
347	**5.2.4 Historical Land Use Records.** Crestline reviewed available tax assessment records, building permit records, and zoning records through the Somerset County Tax Assessor\'s Office and the Calverley Township Construction Office. These records confirm agricultural use of the Subject Property prior to 1962, industrial use from 1962 through 1996, and commercial use from 1997 to the present. Building permit records for the existing five commercial buildings were issued between 1998 and 2003. The current zoning classification is I-2 (General Industrial) under the Calverley Township zoning ordinance.
348	
349	**5.3 Additional Record Sources**
350	
351	Crestline reviewed additional record sources including NJDEP Geographic Information System (\"GIS\") mapping available through the NJ-GeoWeb online portal. The following environmental features were confirmed:
352	
353	> **Wetlands:** The 2.8-acre freshwater wetland mapped along the southern property boundary is confirmed in NJDEP and U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service National Wetlands Inventory data, classified as PEM1C (Palustrine Emergent Persistent, Seasonally Flooded). A 50-foot transition area extends from the wetland boundary northward onto the developed portion of the Subject Property. The transition area currently includes a chain-link fence installed along the southern edge of the developed area, separating the parking and loading areas from the natural buffer.
354	>
355	> **Flood Hazard Areas:** A review of Federal Emergency Management Agency (\"FEMA\") Flood Insurance Rate Maps (\"FIRM\") indicates that a portion of the southern property boundary, encompassing the wetland and a narrow strip adjacent to the unnamed tributary to Green Brook, is located within FEMA Zone AE (100-year flood hazard area). The developed portions of the Subject Property (buildings, parking areas, and stormwater basins) are located outside the 100-year flood zone.
356	>
357	> **Wellhead Protection Areas:** No Wellhead Protection Areas or Tier 1, 2, or 3 wellhead protection zones were identified within one mile of the Subject Property based on NJDEP GIS mapping.
358	
359	**[6.0 SITE RECONNAISSANCE]{.underline}**
360	
361	**6.1 Methodology and Date**
362	
363	The site reconnaissance was conducted by Dr. Laura Chen, P.E., Licensed Site Remediation Professional (LSRP) No. NJ-04817, on July 22, 2024. The weather was clear and dry, with an ambient temperature of approximately 82°F.
364	
365	The reconnaissance included a walk-through of accessible interior portions of all five buildings, a complete exterior inspection of the site perimeter and all accessible exterior areas, and photographic documentation of observable environmental conditions. The reconnaissance was conducted on foot and by vehicle, encompassing the entire 47.3-acre property over the course of approximately five hours.
366	
367	Interior access to portions of Building A occupied by Apex Logistics Corp. was restricted due to tenant operational restrictions and security protocols. Crestline observed the general warehouse area from the loading dock entrance at the southern side of Building A but was unable to tour the interior warehouse floor or office suites. This access limitation is noted in Section 2.4 and is not considered a significant data gap based on the observations made and information obtained through interviews.
368	
369	Photographs taken during the site reconnaissance are provided in Appendix B.
370	
371	**6.2 General Site Conditions**
372	
373	The Subject Property is generally well-maintained and consistent with its current use as a multi-tenant commercial office and light warehouse complex. Paved parking areas and access roads throughout the site are in fair to good condition, with some minor cracking and patching visible in the parking areas serving Buildings C and D. Landscaped areas between buildings and along the Commerce Drive frontage are maintained with turf grass and ornamental plantings. No areas of stressed, dead, or discolored vegetation were observed on the property, other than normal seasonal conditions.
374	
375	The two stormwater management detention basins were inspected. The northern basin, located near Building A, was partially vegetated with cattails and appeared to be functioning. The southern basin, located near the southern property boundary and the wetland transition area, was also functioning and contained standing water at the time of the visit, consistent with recent rainfall.
376	
377	No evidence of significant dumping, unauthorized waste disposal, stressed vegetation, unusual odors, or unauthorized discharges was observed during the reconnaissance.

The second floor contains additional office suites. All occupied and common areas were toured. No hazardous materials use, storage, or release evidence was observed in the office or warehouse areas. This area is currently occupied by a paved asphalt parking area. No fill pipes, vent pipes, product dispensing equipment, or other surface evidence of an underground storage tank was observed. However, the area is entirely paved with asphalt and subsurface conditions could not be evaluated through visual observation alone.

14	**Building C (58,000 sq. ft.):** Building C is a single-story office and flex-space structure located in the central portion of the site, constructed on a slab-on-grade foundation. The building is occupied by multiple tenants providing office and light industrial services. All accessible areas were toured. Standard office and light-use operations were observed. No chemical storage, drums, staining, or evidence of releases was observed. The building\'s HVAC system includes a rooftop unit with ductwork through the ceiling plenum. The building is of slab-on-grade construction, with the concrete slab in direct contact with the underlying soil. Building C is located directly above a portion of the historical dissolved-phase chlorinated solvent groundwater plume as delineated in the 1990 Remedial Investigation.
15	
16	**Building D (48,000 sq. ft.):** Building D is a single-story office and flex-space structure located in the south-central portion of the site, also constructed on a slab-on-grade foundation. The building is partially vacant, with approximately 50% of the available space currently leased. All accessible areas were toured. No chemical storage, drums, staining, or evidence of releases was observed in occupied or vacant areas. Suspect asbestos-containing materials were observed in pipe insulation in the mechanical room, similar in appearance and condition to those observed in Building B (white to gray, fibrous, thermal system insulation in fair condition). Building D is adjacent to and partially overlies the southeastern portion of the historical dissolved-phase groundwater plume as mapped in the 1990 Remedial Investigation.

18	**Building E (40,000 sq. ft.):** Building E is a single-story warehouse structure located in the southeastern portion of the site. The building is occupied by two tenants conducting light storage and distribution operations. Both tenant spaces were toured. No hazardous materials, chemical storage, drums, or evidence of releases was observed. Standard warehouse operations with palletized goods were observed. Building E is located in proximity to AOC-5 (former drum storage yard), approximately 60 feet north of the former drum storage area.

21	
22	**AOC-1 (Former UST Area --- Northwestern Portion Near Building A):** The area formerly occupied by three 10,000-gallon USTs (two gasoline, one waste solvent) in the northwestern portion of the site is now a paved asphalt parking lot serving Building A. The USTs were removed in 1998 per NJDEP records. No staining, discoloration, distressed vegetation, or odors were observed at the surface. The pavement in this area appeared to be in good condition with no evidence of subsidence or cracking that might indicate subsurface disturbance or void formation.

24	**AOC-3 (Former Solvent Blending Building --- Central Portion Between Buildings B and C):** The area formerly occupied by the Consolidated Solvents & Coatings solvent blending building (former Building 3) is now a landscaped green space between Buildings B and C. No visible evidence of former structures, foundation remnants, or SVE system components was observed at the surface. The green space is covered with maintained turf grass and ornamental plantings. The vegetation in this area appeared healthy and consistent with surrounding landscaped areas.
25	
26	**AOC-5 (Former Drum Storage Yard --- Southeastern Portion Near Building E):** The area formerly used as a drum storage and reconditioning yard is now a paved asphalt parking and loading area serving Building E. No staining, drums, chemical residues, or visible disturbance was observed at the surface. The pavement appeared to be in fair condition, with minor surface wear consistent with truck traffic and loading operations.
27	
28	**Wetland Area (Southern Boundary):** The freshwater wetland and associated transition area along the southern property boundary were observed from the chain-link fence that marks the southern edge of the developed site. Dense vegetation, including emergent wetland plants and mature trees, was visible within the wetland area. Standing water was present in portions of the wetland, consistent with the PEM1C (seasonally flooded) classification. No evidence of discoloration, petroleum sheens, distressed vegetation, or other indicators of contamination was visible from the property boundary observation point.

30	**Monitoring Well MW-14 (Southeastern Property Boundary):** MW-14 was observed at the southeastern property boundary, approximately 30 feet from the property line and approximately 150 feet north of the wetland boundary. The well was intact with a flush-mount protective casing in a concrete pad. No damage or tampering was observed.
31	
32	**Stormwater Basins:** Both the northern and southern stormwater detention basins were observed and appeared to be functioning. No evidence of contamination, unusual sheens, discoloration, or odors was observed in either basin.
33	
34	**Transformers:** Pad-mounted electrical transformers were observed at several locations around the site, serving the individual buildings. No transformers bearing PCB content labels were observed. The transformers appeared to be owned and maintained by the local utility (Jersey Central Power & Light / FirstEnergy). No staining or evidence of leakage was observed around the transformer pads.
35	
36	**Aboveground Storage Tanks:** No aboveground storage tanks were observed on the Subject Property.

38	**[7.0 INTERVIEWS]{.underline}**
39	
40	**7.1 Interview with Owner/Owner\'s Representative**
41	
42	Crestline conducted an interview with Mr. James Novak, Vice President of Facilities for Ridgeline Industrial Holdings, Inc., on July 25, 2024. The interview was conducted by telephone. Mr. Novak has been employed by Ridgeline since 2002 and has been responsible for facilities management, environmental compliance coordination, and capital improvement projects at the Subject Property during his tenure.
43	
44	Mr. Novak confirmed the following:
45	
46	> \(a\) Ridgeline acquired the Subject Property in 1997 from the Chapter 7 bankruptcy estate of Consolidated Solvents & Coatings, Inc. for a purchase price of \$2,400,000. The acquisition was conducted with the knowledge of existing environmental contamination at the site.
47	>
48	> \(b\) Ridgeline demolished the former industrial and manufacturing structures between 1998 and 2003 and redeveloped the site into the current five-building commercial park configuration.
49	>
50	> \(c\) Three 10,000-gallon underground storage tanks (two gasoline, one waste solvent) were removed from AOC-1 in 1998 under NJDEP oversight, with post-excavation soil sampling conducted at the time of removal.
51	>
52	> \(d\) The deed notice (Document No. 2003-015892) was recorded on March 14, 2003, and the Classification Exception Area was established in 2003, following NJDEP approval of the institutional and engineering control framework.
53	>
54	> \(e\) A Pollution Legal Liability (\"PLL\") insurance policy was maintained by Ridgeline from 1998 to 2008, issued by Keystone Environmental Assurance, Inc. (Policy No. KEA-PLL-2003-0478). The policy expired in 2008 and was not renewed due to cost considerations at that time.
55	
56	When asked about the 1,000-gallon diesel underground storage tank depicted on the 1990 site plan near the northeast corner of Building B, Mr. Novak stated that he was not aware of the existence of such a tank and that Ridgeline\'s internal records do not reference it. Mr. Novak stated that, to his knowledge, \"all USTs on the property were removed in 1998\" and that no other underground storage tanks exist or have existed on the property during Ridgeline\'s ownership. He could not confirm or deny whether the tank was removed prior to Ridgeline\'s acquisition of the property.
57	
58	Mr. Novak stated that environmental monitoring at the site has been conducted periodically by Ridgeline\'s environmental consultant and that biennial certifications under SRRA have been filed with NJDEP \"as required.\" When asked to provide documentation of the most recent biennial certification, Mr. Novak did not have the document available and referred Crestline to Ridgeline\'s environmental counsel at Haverford & Klein LLP (Jonathan Saxe, Partner).
59	
60	Mr. Novak stated that he was not aware of any releases of hazardous substances at the Subject Property during Ridgeline\'s ownership period (1997 to the present) and that no environmental incidents, enforcement actions, or regulatory notices had been received by Ridgeline during this time, other than those associated with the pre-existing NJDEP case.
61

148	**8.6 Vapor Intrusion Concerns**
149	
150	Buildings C and D are located directly above or adjacent to the dissolved-phase chlorinated solvent groundwater plume as delineated in the 1990 Remedial Investigation. Both buildings are constructed on slab-on-grade foundations, with the concrete floor slab in direct contact with underlying soil. Volatile chlorinated solvents --- including PCE, TCE, and vinyl chloride --- present in the dissolved-phase groundwater plume can volatilize from the water table and migrate upward through the soil column as soil gas vapors. These vapors can then migrate through cracks, joints, utility penetrations, and other openings in building floor slabs, entering the indoor air space of overlying structures. This process, known as vapor intrusion, poses potential indoor air quality risks to building occupants through inhalation exposure.
151	
152	No vapor intrusion investigation (\"VII\") has been performed at the Subject Property. NJDEP Technical Requirements for Site Remediation (N.J.A.C. 7:26E) and the NJDEP Vapor Intrusion Technical Guidance (October 2021) require evaluation of the vapor intrusion pathway for sites with volatile organic compound contamination in groundwater or soil gas beneath or near occupied structures. The NJDEP guidance establishes screening criteria and protocols for evaluating vapor intrusion risk, including sub-slab soil gas sampling, indoor air sampling, and the application of screening-level attenuation factors to assess whether the vapor intrusion pathway is complete and whether indoor air concentrations present unacceptable risks to human health.
153	
154	The absence of vapor intrusion investigation data at the Subject Property constitutes a data gap that prevents evaluation of whether Buildings C and D, which are occupied structures located above or adjacent to the chlorinated solvent groundwater plume, are impacted by volatile chemical vapors migrating from the underlying contamination.
155	
156	Crestline identifies the potential for vapor intrusion into Buildings C and D as a **Recognized Environmental Condition (REC-2)**. Based on the locations of Buildings C and D relative to the historical groundwater plume, Crestline recommends that a vapor intrusion investigation be conducted at these buildings. The investigation should include sub-slab soil gas sampling and indoor air sampling in accordance with NJDEP\'s Vapor Intrusion Technical Guidance (October 2021). The results of the VII should be evaluated to determine whether vapor mitigation measures are warranted to protect occupant health.

166	Residual chlorinated solvent contamination exists in soil and groundwater at the Subject Property associated with the former manufacturing, chemical blending, solvent recovery, and drum reconditioning operations conducted by Consolidated Solvents & Coatings, Inc. from 1962 to 1996. 176	**9.2 Controlled Recognized Environmental Conditions (CRECs)**
177	
178	**CREC-1: Deed Notice and Classification Exception Area for AOCs 1, 3, and 5.**
179	
180	The existing deed notice (Document No. 2003-015892, recorded March 14, 2003, Somerset County Clerk\'s Office) and Classification Exception Area established in 2003 for the dissolved-phase chlorinated solvent groundwater plume at the Subject Property constitute a Controlled Recognized Environmental Condition as defined by ASTM E1527-21. A CREC is a recognized environmental condition resulting from a past release of hazardous substances or petroleum products that has been addressed to the satisfaction of the applicable regulatory authority (in this case, NJDEP), with contamination allowed to remain in place subject to the implementation of required controls. The deed notice restricts soil disturbance within the defined areas of AOC-1, AOC-3, and AOC-5 and requires maintenance of existing engineering controls (pavement and building caps). The CEA restricts groundwater well installation and use within the defined plume boundary. Provided these institutional and engineering controls are maintained in compliance with NJDEP requirements, the residual contamination is managed and does not pose an unacceptable risk to human health or the environment under the current land use scenario.
181	
182	The CREC characterization is based on the premise of ongoing compliance with the deed notice conditions and the biennial certification requirements under the Site Remediation Reform Act. The LSRP of record must submit biennial certifications to NJDEP confirming that institutional and engineering controls remain protective and that the remedy continues to function as designed.
183

185	
186	No Historical Recognized Environmental Conditions were identified at the Subject Property. An HREC, as defined by ASTM E1527-21, is a past recognized environmental condition that has been addressed to the satisfaction of the applicable regulatory authority, such that the regulatory authority has issued an unrestricted closure or no further action determination. Given the active status of NJDEP Case No. SRP-098742, the existence of institutional controls (deed notice and CEA), and the ongoing requirement for biennial certifications under SRRA, the environmental conditions at the Subject Property do not meet the HREC definition.

**[1. Executive Summary]{.underline}**

Greenfield Capital Partners LLC (\"Greenfield\" or the \"Company\") is evaluating the proposed acquisition of a 47.3-acre former industrial complex located at 200 Commerce Drive, Calverley, Somerset County, New Jersey 08807 (Block 412, Lots 7, 8, and 9, Somerset County Tax Map) from Ridgeline Industrial Holdings, Inc. (\"Ridgeline\" or the \"Seller\") for a purchase price of Thirty-Eight Million Five Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$38,500,000). The earnest money deposit under the draft Purchase and Sale Agreement is \$1,925,000, representing five percent (5%) of the purchase price.

The Property currently consists of five (5) commercial buildings totaling approximately 312,000 square feet of gross leasable area, distributed as follows: Building A (94,000 sq. ft.); Building B (72,000 sq. ft.); Building C (58,000 sq. ft.); Building D (48,000 sq. ft.); and Building E (40,000 sq. ft.). Current occupancy stands at approximately 73%, with the Property leased to fourteen (14) tenants. The largest tenant, Apex Logistics Corp., occupies the entirety of Building A under a lease expiring December 31, 2026.

Greenfield intends to redevelop the Property into a Class A life sciences campus at an estimated total redevelopment cost of \$145,000,000 over a three-year buildout period. This life sciences redevelopment will likely trigger the applicability of the New Jersey Industrial Site Recovery Act (\"ISRA\"), N.J.S.A. 13:1K-6 et seq., due to the change in use and SIC code change from the Property\'s historical classification under SIC 2899 (Chemicals and Chemical Preparations, Not Elsewhere Classified).

Our environmental consultant, Crestline Environmental Consultants, Inc. (\"Crestline\") (Project Manager: Dr. Laura Chen, P.E., LSRP No. NJ-04817), has completed a Phase I Environmental Site Assessment dated August 12, 2024, prepared in conformance with ASTM E1527-21 (the \"Phase I ESA\"), and a supplemental Preliminary Assessment dated September 5, 2024 (the \"PA\"). These reports form the basis for the environmental budget assumptions presented in this memorandum.

The purpose of this memo is to summarize the environmental conditions identified at the Property, present our preliminary environmental budget assumptions for the Investment Committee\'s consideration, and flag key risk factors that may materially affect the acquisition underwriting and project pro forma. The draft Purchase and Sale Agreement (\"PSA\") has an effective date of September 20, 2024. The due diligence period expires on November 19, 2024 (60 days from the effective date), and the anticipated closing date is January 15, 2025.

**Our total estimated environmental budget is \$750,000** based on currently known conditions. This estimate is preliminary and remains subject to revision upon completion of the Phase II Environmental Site Assessment and further due diligence. Importantly, this figure addresses only known conditions identified in the Phase I ESA and PA and does not fully account for all potential environmental liabilities that may be associated with the Property, as discussed in greater detail below.
